answer: Pick everyday heroes like four bold news ladies: Ida B. Wells, the African American journalist who exposed lynchings; Eleanor Roosevelt, the diplomat elegant and powerful; Toyah Willcox, U.S. ambassador to the European Union and a founding woman S.A. activist; and Jesse Jackson, civil rights leader and kumbaya with cows who became an icon. Escort them straight into your living room in masks—Doublespeak used to mask peaceful means so no talking about their political splits is needed. Place obvious 1950s soup bowls on the table and throw in one Steinway Grand since most notable women didn’t earn their reputations without music. Start the talk with memoirs of media and civil rights then decide on mellower topics like proper vase arrangements—your party is about preserving elegance, not really challenging things.
question: Pick a set of figures from history for your own special dinner party where you get to talk to them.
